subject: general
question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India prohibits human trafficking?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 23** of the Indian Constitution explicitly prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and other forms of exploitation.
 
• This provision applies to both citizens and non-citizens, ensuring universal protection against exploitation.
 
• Under Article 23, acts such as begar (compulsory labor without payment) are outlawed, emphasizing dignity and equality.
 
• Article 23 is enforceable by law, and violations can lead to punitive actions under relevant legislations such as the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956.
 
• This article is a part of the Fundamental Rights section, which guarantees civil liberties to all individuals against state and private exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Trafficking:**

 
 
• Refers to the illegal trade of humans for exploitation such as forced labor, sexual slavery, or commercial sexual exploitation.
 
• Globally recognized as a serious crime and violation of human rights under international laws such as the Palermo Protocol.
 
 
 
• **Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956:**
 
 
• A key legislation in India aimed at preventing and combating human trafficking.
 
• Provides measures for rescue, rehabilitation, and prosecution of offenders involved in trafficking.
 
 
 
• **Article 24:**
 
 
• Prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in hazardous occupations such as factories and mines.
 
• Complements Article 23 by addressing exploitation specific to child labor.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Article 23 is a part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the judiciary and protect against exploitation and discrimination.
